title: Downtown renewal: streetscaping, waste and washrooms
subtitle: Also covered: first Indigenous Relations Framework, downtown heritage district study, recycling audit, and a federal grant closed session.
overview: The committee spent most of the afternoon on a package of downtown renewal reports. It recommended an enhanced streetscape for the Downtown Infrastructure Renewal Program, with faster construction on Wyndham Street North to shorten disruption for businesses. It also recommended better downtown waste collection, including underground communal containers, and a series of steps to expand public washrooms, including a self-cleaning washroom at Wyndham Street and St. George's Square.

The committee recommended approval of the City's first Indigenous Relations Framework {{vote:m2}}, a five-year guide for the City's work on reconciliation. It also recommended that staff prepare a plan and guidelines for a Downtown Guelph Heritage Conservation District {{vote:m16}}, and it received a value-for-money audit of the recycling program transition {{vote:m3}}.

The streetscape, waste and washroom items carry costs that would only proceed if adopted in the 2025 budget confirmation. Staff said project deferrals will be needed to make room for them and will be shared in the fall. Earlier, the mayor reported that Council received information and gave staff direction on a federal grant agreement after a closed session. All of these recommendations still go to Council.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the City's first Indigenous Relations Framework, which sets commitments for the next five years.

The committee recommended an enhanced level of service for downtown waste, with enhanced public space containers and communal underground containers, subject to adoption of the estimated $1.0 million project budget and $410,000 operating increase in the 2025 budget confirmation.

The committee recommended an enhanced streetscape prioritizing trees, flexible streets, seating and paving stones, subject to the estimated $17.1 million increase in the 2025 budget, and directed staff to design and tender Wyndham Street North for expedited construction.

The committee recommended a package of washroom measures, including underground infrastructure in each downtown phase, a Community Toilet Scheme with the Downtown Guelph Business Association, and prioritizing accessible and gender-neutral options.
The committee recommended that staff include a self-cleaning public washroom in the Wyndham Street and St. George's Square redevelopment, subject to the 2025 budget confirmation.

The committee recommended that staff explore water fountains or refill stations with future washrooms, and temporary options in the interim, subject to consultation with public health and future budgets.
The committee recommended that staff discuss an innovation opportunity with the University of Guelph on a fluid alternative to perfumed portable toilet products, and report back to Council.
The committee recommended approving the heritage district study's recommendations and directed staff to prepare a plan and guideline for the district under the Ontario Heritage Act.

debate: Delegates on the Indigenous Relations Framework raised concerns about how the process was run, including the City's handling of a community ceremony and sacred fire site, and called for a community-led process. Another delegate said the City should comply with treaty obligations, including in its water and wastewater approvals. Staff said the framework is a starting point and that the advisory circle's form still needs research.

On recycling, one councillor questioned why downtown would get extended collection for one year only. Staff said the transition gives time to address materials that do not fit the provincial program, and that the user fee item is only a study, not a decision to impose fees.

On the budget, one councillor was hesitant to support the downtown items without knowing which projects would be deferred, and asked about a major east-end road project. Staff said that project was not affected so far, that the decisions are policy direction only, and that deferral details will come with the budget in the fall.

On the self-cleaning washroom, one councillor proposed instead having staff study it and report back, citing accessibility concerns about perfumed and chemical products. Others said staff would already review accessibility through detailed design and the Accessibility Advisory Committee, and that reporting back could slow the project. That amendment was defeated {{vote:m10}}.

On the heritage district, one councillor worried it could add complexity for developers. Staff said downtown already has many listed and designated properties and that landowners would be notified, while other councillors said heritage supports downtown business and tourism.
